CHM-N-001.title: winning guy
CHM-N-001.body:
huh?

Purpose: Keep old friends together through a change. Gift to others: Permission to be ordinary and imperfect.

Their voice: We all have a part to do; I will take this one.

Under pressure: An old friend wants to grow beyond the group’s familiar habits. Pushed too far (Slob): Refuse a useful change because the familiar way is easier. Disconnected from their gift (Snob): Keep a newcomer outside because they lack the right background.

Another side: Companion + Warrior = Ally

Defend someone who cannot defend themselves

They watch what happens and choose their moment to respond. They notice the small details and want to know how each step works. They pay particular attention to the people around them and their surroundings. They weigh their own judgment alongside evidence and advice from others. They find common ground first, then draw attention to the exceptions. They prefer room to explore alternatives and find their own way forward. To get through to them, it helps to offer facts they can check. In a disagreement, they step back to consider what an outside observer would see.

They notice Loud or sudden sounds (brief pause). They notice Vibration (full concentration). They notice Pressure or discomfort (strong attention). They notice Noticeable objects (brief pause). They notice Gestures or facial expressions (passing glance). They notice Distinctive colours (strong attention).

They place trust in an institution and expertise.

Belonging matters through belonging to several groups. Their relationships give or risk a voice in decisions. Their usual place in a group is a member.

Their recurring feelings include pride, shame and hope.

choices: Help an outsider become part of a group

questions.prompt: How does this side show in their behaviour?
questions.hint: Show loyalty, authenticity and practical sharing in a specific interaction.
choices: Do an unglamorous part of the work without making a show of it
Make room for someone who feels out of place
Admit an ordinary mistake so others can be themselves

questions.prompt: What do other people receive from them?
questions.hint: The Companion offers fellowship, acceptance and space for human imperfection.
choices: A circle where someone feels included
Loyal practical help from an equal
Permission to be ordinary and imperfect

questions.prompt: What might they actually say?
questions.hint: Their voice puts people on equal ground and brings grand claims back to everyday reality.
choices: Sit with us. You do not have to impress anyone here.
We all have a part to do; I will take this one.
Let us say what we mean and work it out together.

questions.prompt: What puts their gift or purpose under pressure?
questions.hint: Test the difference between belonging, settling for too little and looking down on others.
choices: An old friend wants to grow beyond the group’s familiar habits
A newcomer challenges the group’s unspoken rules
A chance to gain status would separate them from their friends

questions.prompt: Slob: what happens when they push this side too far?
questions.hint: Slob: Comfort and fitting in become complacency, lack of effort or resistance to anyone aiming higher.
choices: Dismiss a friend’s ambition as showing off
Let others do the shared work while taking belonging for granted
Refuse a useful change because the familiar way is easier

questions.prompt: Snob: what happens when they lose touch with this gift?
questions.hint: Snob: Equality gives way to distance, superiority or selective belonging.
choices: Keep a newcomer outside because they lack the right background
Treat old friends as embarrassing after gaining status
Offer friendship only to people who improve their position

questions.prompt: What does another archetype bring to this character?
questions.hint: Optional: choose a second lens, then adapt the combination in your own words. The order matters: the main archetype remains the foundation. A combination label is a writing prompt, not a new compulsory character type.

CHAR-INPUT-2.title: NLP Meta Programs — Preference Spectra
CHAR-INPUT-2.body: They watch what happens and choose their moment to respond. They notice the small details and want to know how each step works. They pay particular attention to the people around them and their surroundings. They weigh their own judgment alongside evidence and advice from others. They find common ground first, then draw attention to the exceptions. They prefer room to explore alternatives and find their own way forward. To get through to them, it helps to offer facts they can check. In a disagreement, they step back to consider what an outside observer would see.

reference.title: NLP Meta Programs — Preference Spectra
reference.body: NLP Meta Programs as character-writing prompts: explore how a character approaches a situation across six independent paired preferences.

ACT-2.body: The teams search the warehouse and recover the Cipher-Key.
ACT-2.phaseNotes: Role pressure phase: practical leaders, scouts, solvers, and cautious players start becoming visible.

ACT-3.title: Act 3 - The Decode
ACT-3.body: The Dataslate reveals the route and the deeper Chimera secret.
ACT-3.phaseNotes: Cooperation phase: teams must combine clues and notice whether specialists share control or hoard it.

ACT-4.title: Act 4 - The Turn
ACT-4.body: The false-flag intercept reframes who the teams can trust.
ACT-4.phaseNotes: Stress phase: trust, suspicion, and group hierarchy become explicit under uncertainty.

ACT-5.title: Act 5 - Extraction
ACT-5.body: The teams call the beacon and escape before the operation collapses.
ACT-5.phaseNotes: Resolution phase: teams commit to a shared plan and reveal whether their earlier roles still hold.
